items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC proposes first substantive update to transfer agent rules since the early 1980s, citing blockchain use in share transfers
items.facts: On September 1, 2026 the SEC issued Release 2026-81 proposing to update the rules and forms that apply to registered transfer agents. The release states that the Commission's transfer agent rules "have not been substantively updated since the first rules were adopted in the late 1970s and early 1980s." SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins is quoted saying the proposal "would streamline and modernize the Commission's rules to reflect transfer agents' current processes and operations, including the use of electronic communications and blockchain technology in connection with securities offerings and the transfer of shares." The release states the proposal would amend existing rules and forms, would rescind a rule, and would introduce new rules applying to registered transfer agents and their activities. The proposing release is numbered 34-106246. According to the release, the proposal will be published in the Federal Register and the public comment period will remain open for 60 days after the date of that publication; as of this entry the proposal had not yet appeared in the Federal Register, so the comment period closing date is not yet fixed.
items.source_label: SEC Press Release 2026-81
items.relevant_to: transfer agents, issuers using blockchain-based share registers, tokenized-securities platforms, clearing and settlement operators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)
items.title: FinCEN section 311 special-measure proposal on Banque Misr UAE published in the Federal Register; comments close October 1, 2026
items.facts: FinCEN's notice of proposed rulemaking, "Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Banque Misr UAE as a Financial Institution Operating Outside of the United States of Primary Money Laundering Concern," was published in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026 (document 2026-17871, citation 91 FR 56085). The Federal Register record lists the comment period as closing on October 1, 2026. The published abstract states that FinCEN "is issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, that finds the five United Arab Emirates-based branches of Banque Misr (collectively, Banque Misr UAE) to be of primary money laundering concern" and proposes a special measure to "prohibit U.S. financial institutions from opening or maintaining a correspondent account for, or on behalf of, Banque Misr UAE," to "require U.S. financial institutions to take reasonable steps not to process a transaction for the correspondent account in the United States of a foreign banking institution if such a transaction involves Banque Misr UAE," and to "require U.S. financial institutions to apply special due diligence to their foreign correspondent accounts that are reasonably designed to guard against their use to process transactions involving Banque Misr UAE." The underlying proposal was announced by Treasury on August 28, 2026.
items.source_label: Federal Register, 91 FR 56085 (FinCEN proposed rule)
items.relevant_to: banks and money services businesses with correspondent banking exposure, payment processors, BSA/AML compliance teams

items.issuing_body: Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
items.title: CFTC settles insider-trading charges over prediction-market event contracts, ordering $172,000 and a three-year trading ban
items.facts: In Release Number 9289-26, dated August 28, 2026, the CFTC announced an order filing and settling charges against Gabriel Perez for misappropriating material, nonpublic information obtained through his federal government employment in order to trade event contracts (i.e., swaps) on a prediction market platform for his personal benefit. Under the order, Perez must disgorge profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil monetary penalty of $65,000, which the CFTC describes as a substantial discount under the Division of Enforcement's new cooperation advisory because of Perez's cooperation; Perez agreed to cease and desist from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations, and a three-year trading ban is imposed. The order finds that between December 2025 and February 2026, while working as a teleprompter operator for the White House, Perez traded presidential mention market contracts, which are event contracts reflecting words or phrases the President may use during his speeches, generating over $107,500 in profits. The CFTC states that it appreciates the assistance of KalshiEX in this matter.
items.source_label: CFTC Release Number 9289-26 (August 28, 2026)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, designated contract markets, event-contract intermediaries, trading-surveillance and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury (FinCEN and OFAC)
items.title: FinCEN proposes a USA PATRIOT Act section 311 special measure to cut off Banque Misr UAE's U.S. correspondent banking access
items.facts: On August 28, 2026, Treasury announced that FinCEN issued a notice of proposed rulemaking finding that Banque Misr in the United Arab Emirates is a financial institution operating outside the United States of primary money laundering concern. Pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, FinCEN proposes prohibiting U.S. financial institutions from opening or maintaining a correspondent account for, or on behalf of, Banque Misr UAE. Treasury states the rule would also require U.S. financial institutions to take reasonable steps not to process a transaction for a correspondent account in the United States of a foreign banking institution if such a transaction involves Banque Misr UAE, and to apply to their foreign correspondent accounts special due diligence reasonably designed to guard against their use to process transactions involving Banque Misr UAE. Treasury states the public comment period will close 30 days after the NPRM is published in the Federal Register, and that the finding and proposed special measure apply only to Banque Misr UAE and not to Banque Misr operations in any other country. Treasury estimates that between January 2024 and June 2026, Banque Misr UAE processed approximately $1.8 billion for 103 companies that are potentially part of Iranian shadow banking networks. Separately, OFAC sanctioned Reza Mohammad Taeedi, described as the general manager of Bank Melli's Dubai branch, and Hong Kong-based Kameng Trading Limited, which Treasury states was used by sanctioned Iranian exchange house Pedram Pirouzan Exchange House to launder money for Iran.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release sb0617 (August 28, 2026)
items.relevant_to: banks and money transmitters with correspondent relationships, payment processors, BSA/AML and sanctions-screening teams

items.issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
items.title: SEC charges 38 entities with using false Forms ADV to pose as legitimate U.S. advisory firms
items.facts: On August 27, 2026, in Release 2026-78, the SEC charged 38 entities alleging that they made material misrepresentations in Forms ADV filed with the Commission between 2025 and 2026 to falsely portray themselves as legitimate advisory firms to U.S. investors, and that a number of them used IP addresses tracked to foreign jurisdictions to connect to the Commission's filing system. Laura D'Allaird, Chief of the SEC Enforcement Division's Cyber and Emerging Technologies Unit, is quoted stating that the complaints allege large-scale abuse of SEC adviser filings by persons, several of whom are likely located overseas, exploiting interest in emerging technologies. According to the complaints, the defendants listed places of business at addresses in Colorado where they had no presence, provided phone numbers that are disconnected or belong to unrelated businesses, disclosed ownership structures and numerical data identical or nearly identical to a multitude of other purported exempt reporting advisers, and claimed audits by one of two independent public accounting firms that cannot be found in any public registry of federal or state accountancy firms. The SEC also alleges certain defendants were marketed on websites, some displaying a fake certificate indicating SEC registration. The complaints, filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, charge violations of Sections 204(a) and 207 of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The SEC states the ERA filings of the 38 entities have been removed from the Commission website, and that its Office of Investor Education and Assistance issued an investor alert warning that scammers are using SEC ERA filings to create a false impression of legitimacy.
items.source_label: SEC Press Release 2026-78 (August 27, 2026)
items.relevant_to: crypto and fintech platforms whose counterparties cite SEC filings, exempt reporting advisers, retail-facing investment platforms, compliance and diligence teams

items.issuing_body: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
items.title: SEC notices MEMX proposal to list and trade 'securities event contracts' on a national securities exchange
items.facts: The Federal Register published on August 27, 2026 an SEC Notice of Filing of a proposed rule change (Release No. 34-106182, File No. SR-MEMX-2026-25; SEC notice dated August 24, 2026; filed by MEMX on August 11, 2026) in which MEMX LLC proposes to adopt new Chapter 30 of the Exchange Rules to provide for the listing and trading of securities event contracts on the Exchange's options platform, MEMX Options. The filing states that prediction markets recently have experienced significant growth and that these markets generally have developed on exchanges regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission as designated contract markets. The filing describes securities event contracts as cash-settled, European-style binary options that are based on the outcome of an event question related to the financial performance of an issuer of an NMS stock. The Commission is soliciting comments on the proposed rule change.
items.source_label: Federal Register, SEC Release No. 34-106182, File No. SR-MEMX-2026-25 (published August 27, 2026)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, options and equities market participants, exchange and broker-dealer product teams

items.issuing_body: New York State Department of State, Division of Consumer Protection (published on the NYDFS newsroom)
items.title: New York consumer alert on AI-driven investment scams names fake cryptocurrency projects and routes virtual-currency complaints to NYDFS
items.facts: On August 27, 2026, the New York State Department of State's Division of Consumer Protection issued an alert urging New Yorkers to remain vigilant against increasingly sophisticated investment scams driven by artificial intelligence. The release cites Federal Trade Commission data that 144,041 consumers reported losing over $8 billion to investment scams in 2025, a 38% increase from 2024, with a median loss of $10,560. Among the scam categories the alert enumerates are fake cryptocurrency projects, and among the warning signs it lists opportunities that require payments using cryptocurrency or wire transfers. The alert directs consumers to report cryptocurrency fraud or file a complaint against a virtual currency company in New York State to the Department of Financial Services. The release carries a statement from DFS Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow. The alert is educational guidance and does not announce a rule or an enforcement action.
items.source_label: NYS Department of State Division of Consumer Protection / NYDFS newsroom (August 27, 2026)
items.relevant_to: virtual currency businesses licensed in New York, crypto exchanges and custodians, consumer-facing fintech and payments platforms

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / OFAC
items.title: OFAC names the digital asset sector of Iran's economy in five new E.O. 13902 sectoral sanctions determinations
items.facts: On August 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control issued five sectoral sanctions determinations pursuant to Executive Order 13902, covering the digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors of the Iranian economy. Treasury states that with the action OFAC "can now sanction any person, regardless of where they are located, that operates in" those sectors, and describes the digital assets sector as one where "the Iranian regime increasingly turns to cryptocurrency as a tool of choice for sanctions evasion, supporting transactions linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Iranian regime insiders." Treasury states the announcement "expands secondary sanctions exposure for those who continue doing business with the Iranian regime." The determination document is published by OFAC as "Determination Pursuant to Executive Order 13902 - Aviation, Digital Asset, Gold, Shipping, and Technology Sectors of the Iranian Economy." The determinations were announced as part of what Treasury calls Operation Economic Outcast.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release (sb0613), August 24, 2026
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges and VASPs, stablecoin issuers, payment processors, banks with correspondent exposure, sanctions-screening and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / OFAC
items.title: OFAC's August 24 Iran designations add SDN entries carrying digital currency addresses and cite crypto-facilitated oil payments
items.facts: On August 24, 2026, OFAC added Iran-related names to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List in an action Treasury says sanctioned nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels. The published SDN additions include five "Digital Currency Address" identifiers; one listed individual, Almpertos Tsoris of Greece, appears with "Digital Currency Address - USDT TJCBpxZ3yC7C7oegSRZMFxBcscmUVeSA36" under the [IRAN-EO13902] program tag. Treasury states that Arman Kahzadian, designated pursuant to Executive Order 13694 as further amended, "has focused on digital asset heists" and that "in summer 2023, Arman Kahzadian illicitly gained control of a wallet that held over $30,000 worth of Bitcoin." Treasury also states that UAE-based Ivan Obukhov, designated pursuant to Executive Order 13224, "has processed over 100 million dollars' worth of cryptocurrency payments to facilitate oil sales on behalf of the IRGC-QF" since 2023.
items.source_label: OFAC Recent Actions listing, August 24, 2026
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges and VASPs, blockchain analytics and screening vendors, payment processors, banks and money services businesses

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury
items.title: Treasury launches a financial-sector Quantum-Readiness Task Force with a digital assets workstream
items.facts: On August 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced the launch of the Quantum-Readiness Task Force, following Executive Order 14412. Treasury describes it as "a public-private initiative to help accelerate the U.S. financial sector's transition to quantum-safe technology in an orderly and operationally resilient manner," building on the G7 Cyber Expert Group roadmap for the transition to post-quantum cryptography. Treasury states the Task Force "will operate through three workstreams: Sector Alignment & PQC Transition; Third-Party & Vendor Readiness; and Digital Assets and Emerging Technology Risk," and that future quantum systems "could break many of the cryptographic tools that protect financial data, payment systems, digital identities, and market infrastructure." Treasury states the Task Force will bring together government, financial institutions, financial market infrastructures, technology providers and other private-sector leaders.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release (sb0615), August 24, 2026
items.relevant_to: banks and financial market infrastructures, payment processors, fintech platforms, custodians and digital asset infrastructure providers, vendor-risk teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
items.title: OFAC suspends five Iran general licenses, including the personal-remittances authorization, with a September 8 wind-down
items.facts: In a notice titled "Suspension of Certain Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations General Licenses," OFAC states that on August 24, 2026 it announced it is issuing a rule "suspending indefinitely the effectiveness" of five general licenses issued under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR part 560: 31 CFR 560.544 (certain educational activities by U.S. persons in third countries), 31 CFR 560.550 ("Certain noncommercial, personal remittances to or from Iran authorized"), 31 CFR 560.554 (importation and exportation of services related to conferences), Iran General License F (certain services supporting professional and amateur sports activities and exchanges), and Iran General License G (certain academic exchanges and educational services). The notice states that OFAC is concurrently issuing General License BB, "authorizing all transactions prohibited by the ITSR that are ordinarily incident and necessary to the wind down of any transaction previously authorized by one or more of the above general licenses until September 8, 2026, subject to certain conditions," and that transactions previously authorized under the suspended licenses "are no longer authorized by OFAC, except to the extent authorized pursuant to General License BB until September 8, 2026." The notice directs parties seeking a specific license for covered activity occurring after the effective date of the suspension to OFAC's website.
items.source_label: OFAC — Suspension of Certain Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations General Licenses (notice, Aug. 24, 2026)
items.relevant_to: money transmitters, remittance providers, payment processors, banks with Iran-nexus screening

items.title: OFAC Iran General License BB authorizes wind-down of suspended Iran general licenses, including noncommercial personal remittances, only through 12:01 a.m. EDT on September 8, 2026
items.facts: OFAC General License BB, "Authorizing the Wind Down of Certain Transactions Previously Authorized Under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations," is dated August 24, 2026 and signed by Bradley T. Smith, Director, Office of Foreign Assets Control. Paragraph (a) states that, except as provided in paragraph (b), transactions prohibited by the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations (31 CFR part 560) that are "ordinarily incident and necessary to the wind down" of transactions previously authorized under the listed general licenses "are authorized through 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time, September 8, 2026, provided that any payment to a blocked person is made into a blocked interest-bearing account located in the United States in accordance with the ITSR." The listed authorities are 31 CFR 560.544 (certain educational activities by U.S. persons in third countries), 31 CFR 560.550 (certain noncommercial, personal remittances to or from Iran), 31 CFR 560.554 (services related to conferences in the United States or third countries), Iran General License F (certain services supporting professional and amateur sports activities and exchanges), and Iran General License G (certain academic exchanges and educational services). items.issuing_body: Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC Holds Inaugural Innovation Advisory Committee Meeting Covering Crypto Regulation, AI and Compute in Derivatives Markets, and Prediction Markets and Novel Event Contracts
items.facts: In press release 9288-26, dated August 21, 2026, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission stated that it held the inaugural meeting of its Innovation Advisory Committee in Washington, D.C. on August 20, 2026, and that the Committee was created to advise the Commission on complex issues at the intersection of technology, law, policy, and finance. The release states that IAC Chair Walt Lukken told members that the Committee is there to provide practical advice to the Commission rooted in real world experiences, and that good policy is informed policy which comes from listening to the people who operate, use, and build these markets every day. The release quotes Chairman Selig's opening remarks that it is not a question of whether innovations like blockchain, artificial intelligence, and prediction markets will transform our markets, but a question of where this innovation will take place and who will write the rules. The release states that members discussed topics including crypto's regulatory evolution, artificial intelligence and compute within the derivatives markets, along with prediction markets and the future of novel event contracts, and that Chairman Selig adjourned the meeting at 4:00 p.m. ET.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9288-26 (cftc.gov)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract venues, crypto derivatives operators, exchanges

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control
items.title: OFAC Venezuela General License 61 Excludes Payment Terms Denominated in Venezuelan Government-Issued Digital Currency, Digital Coin or Digital Tokens
items.facts: On August 21, 2026, OFAC issued Venezuela General License 61, authorizing the supply of certain items and services to Venezuela related to telecommunications, and Venezuela General License 62, authorizing negotiations of and entry into contingent contracts for investment in the telecommunications sector of Venezuela, together with one new Venezuela-related Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1266. FAQ 1266 states that GL 61 authorizes transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to the provision from the United States or by a U.S. person of goods, technology, software, or services for the installation, maintenance, refurbishment, repair, upgrade, operation, or support of telecommunications in Venezuela, including transactions involving the Government of Venezuela, including but not limited to CONATEL, CANTV and Movilnet, and that authorized transactions include processing payments and arranging shipping, logistics, warehousing, insurance and delivery services. FAQ 1266 further states that GL 61 does not authorize payment terms that are not commercially reasonable, involve debt swaps or payments in gold, or are denominated in digital currency, digital coin, or digital tokens issued by, for, or on behalf of the Government of Venezuela, including the petro. FAQ 1266 also states that GL 61 does not authorize any transaction involving a person located in or organized under the laws of Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, or the People's Republic of China, or an entity owned or controlled by or in a joint venture with such a person; the unblocking of property blocked pursuant to the Venezuela Sanctions Regulations; transactions involving blocked vessels; or the formation of new joint ventures or other entities in Venezuela to develop or invest in the telecommunications sector.
items.source_label: OFAC Recent Actions 20260821 and associated FAQ 1266 (Treasury/OFAC)
items.relevant_to: payment processors, sanctions-compliance functions, digital-asset service providers, telecommunications suppliers with US nexus

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets published in the Federal Register; comments close October 20, 2026
items.facts: The Securities and Exchange Commission's proposing release titled "Regulation Crypto Assets" was published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026 at 91 FR 54510, spanning pages 54510 to 54655, as document 2026-17183 under Release Nos. 33-11434 and 34-106150, File No. S7-2026-27, RIN 3235-AN38. The document's DATES section states: "This release was published in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026. Comments should be received on or before October 20, 2026." The published summary states that the Commission "is proposing new rules to create a tailored offering regime for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets," and that the proposed rules "would include two exemptions from the registration requirements of section 5 of the Securities Act of 1933. The first exemption would permit offerings of up to $5 million during a four-year period. The second exemption would permit offerings of up to $75 million during each 12-month period. Under both exemptions, issuers would be required to make certain principles-based narrative disclosures available to their investors. In addition, issuers under the second exemption would be required to provide financial statements and would be subject to ongoing reporting requirements. Issuers that rely on these exemptions would remain subject to the antifraud and antimanipulation provisions of the Federal securities laws." The summary further states that the proposed rules "would include a conditional safe harbor from the term 'investment contract' in the definitions of 'security' in the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934," and that if the conditions of that safe harbor are satisfied, "then a crypto asset would be deemed not to be subject to an investment contract for purposes of those definitions of 'security.'" The Commission announced the proposal on August 18, 2026. The proposal is not in effect; it is a proposed rule open for public comment.
items.source_label: Federal Register — SEC proposed rule, 91 FR 54510 (August 21, 2026), document 2026-17183
items.relevant_to: crypto asset issuers, token offering platforms, digital asset exchanges, crypto fund managers, securities counsel

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury
items.title: Treasury announces proposed guidance on eligible investments in Trump Accounts and a designation framework for account trustees
items.facts: On August 20, 2026 the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced proposed guidance governing eligible investments in Trump Accounts, stating the guidance has "a focus on keeping costs low, promoting broad diversification, and helping children's savings grow over the long term." The release states that the proposed guidance "would support the long-term growth of children's Trump Accounts by limiting eligible investments to choices with low expense ratios and excluding products with excessive fees or unnecessarily complex strategies." On scope, the release states: "The proposed guidance establishes a framework for the designation of eligible investments for future Trump Account trustees, including rollover trustees. Under the framework, an eligible index must be designed primarily to measure the performance of a broad segment of the U.S. or global equity market using objective financial criteria." The release notes that Treasury "previously announced that State Street SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 ETF (SPYM) would be the default investment for all Trump Accounts" and "also announced four additional low-cost index ETFs that may be chosen for investment by a parent or other responsible party." Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is quoted stating, "Every dollar in a child's Trump Account should be working toward that child's financial future, not diminished by unnecessary fees." The announcement describes proposed guidance; the retrieved release does not state a comment deadline, docket number or Federal Register citation.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release sb0609 (August 20, 2026)
items.relevant_to: consumer investment platforms, custodians and prospective account trustees, asset managers, fintech savings providers

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control
items.title: OFAC designates ten in a Hizballah cash-courier network that abuses Turkiye-based exchange houses, and re-designates Hizballah under IRGC-Qods Force command
items.facts: OFAC designated 10 individuals that are part of a network responsible for transferring cash to Hizballah. Treasury states the network uses couriers travelling on commercial airline flights between Lebanon, Turkiye, the UAE and Iran to move up to hundreds of millions of dollars between jurisdictions, "providing an avenue outside the formal financial system for Hizballah to obtain foreign currency and evade sanctions." OFAC also re-designated Hizballah for service to the Iranian regime under the command of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force. The release states that Yunus Alper Yilmaz "abuses certain Turkiye-based exchange houses as fronts for his business dealings and provided front companies and bank accounts for money transfers connected with the IRGC-QF," and that associates including couriers Halil Ibrahim Kacmaz and Onder Dede "collect cash from the exchange houses," with Vasfi Akyuz coordinating logistics. The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order 13224, as amended. The corresponding SDN List updates were published the same day.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury press release sb0611, August 20, 2026
items.relevant_to: money services businesses and money transmitters, payment processors, banks and fintechs running sanctions screening, BSA and AML compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC announces supplemental consent orders against former Alameda CEO Caroline Ellison and Alameda and FTX co-founder Gary Wang
items.facts: On August 19, 2026 the CFTC announced the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York entered supplemental consent orders against Caroline Ellison, former Alameda CEO, and Gary Wang, former Alameda and FTX co-founder. The orders require Ellison and Wang to continue cooperating with the Commission, impose a five-year trading ban and a 10-year registration ban on Ellison, and impose a five-year trading ban and an eight-year registration ban on Wang, with the bans running from the date of entry of the initial consent orders entered December 23, 2022. The supplemental orders acknowledge the Commission is not seeking restitution, disgorgement, and/or civil monetary penalties at this time, a decision based in part on the level of Ellison's and Wang's cooperation in the Commission's investigation and related proceedings, including the parallel criminal actions in which each pled guilty to several criminal charges, and the $11.020 billion forfeiture order in those criminal actions for which they were jointly and severally liable. The initial and supplemental consent orders resolve the CFTC's enforcement actions against Ellison and Wang.
items.source_label: CFTC Release 9285-26
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital asset trading firms, enforcement and white-collar counsel

items.title: Comptroller Gould says a GENIUS Act final rule will be out by November and that 23 of 40 new charter applications involve digital asset activity

items.issuing_body: Florida Office of the Attorney General
items.title: Florida Attorney General sues Stake and VGW sweepstakes casino operators and the payment processors that enable them
items.facts: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced the filing of two lawsuits in Hillsborough County Circuit Court against the operators of major online "sweepstakes" casinos, including Stake and VGW's Chumba Casino, LuckyLand and Global Poker, and against the payment processors that enable them. The complaints allege the defendants are operating illegal online gambling enterprises that violate Florida's gambling laws and the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act. According to the complaints, the defendants use a dual-currency model in which players purchase packages of "Gold Coins" bundled with "Stake Cash" or "Sweeps Coins" that function as redeemable wagering credits that can be cashed out for cryptocurrency, gift cards or cash after minimal play-through requirements. The lawsuits seek permanent injunctions prohibiting the defendants from operating or soliciting in Florida, forfeiture and recovery of money lost by Florida consumers, disgorgement, civil penalties under FDUTPA, restitution and attorneys' fees. The announcement does not name individual payment processors; the two complaints are linked from the release.
items.source_label: Florida Office of the Attorney General news release, August 19, 2026
items.relevant_to: sweepstakes and social-casino operators, payment processors and PSPs serving gaming merchants, affiliate and influencer marketers, gaming counsel

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC publishes Cboe BZX proposal to list 3x Bitcoin and 3x Ether ETFs under a rule that prohibits leveraged products; comments due September 9
items.facts: The SEC published notice, under Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 19b-4, of a proposed rule change filed by Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. on August 10, 2026 to list and trade shares of 3x Gold ETF, 3x Silver ETF, 3x Bitcoin ETF, 3x Ether ETF, 3x Crude Oil ETF and 3x Natural Gas ETF, each a series of the VS Trust, under BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4) governing Commodity-Based Trust Shares. Each fund seeks daily results, before fees and expenses, corresponding to three times the daily performance of its reference commodity, measured by a benchmark of first- and second-month futures contracts. The notice states that the funds "do not meet the standard set forth in BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4)(F), which prohibits leveraged products," and that the trust and the funds operate and are registered as commodity pools with the CFTC and are not registered as investment companies under the Investment Company Act of 1940. Volatility Shares LLC is the sponsor. Submissions referring to file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-065 should be submitted on or before September 9, 2026. The Commission will approve, disapprove or institute proceedings within 45 days of publication, extendable to 90 days.
items.source_label: Federal Register, SEC Release No. 34-106137, File No. SR-CboeBZX-2026-065, published August 19, 2026
items.relevant_to: crypto ETP sponsors and issuers, exchanges and market makers, digital-asset fund managers, commodity pool operators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury
items.title: Treasury proposes rules defining when a payment stablecoin is issued, offered or sold in the United States under GENIUS Act section 3; comments close October 19, 2026
items.facts: The U.S. Department of the Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking implementing section 3 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act, announced August 17, 2026 and published in the Federal Register on August 18, 2026 at 91 FR 53368 (document 2026-16796, RIN 1505-AC95, agency docket TREAS-DO-2026-0496, 24 pages). Treasury states that it "proposes to issue regulations to implement section 3 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act regarding the statutory prohibitions and limitations on payment stablecoin issuance, offer, and sale in the United States." The proposal would add a new Part 1523 to 12 CFR Chapter XV, which proposed section 1523.1 states "is issued by Treasury to implement section 3 of the Act (12 U.S.C. 5902) regarding statutory prohibitions and limitations on issuing, offering, selling, and otherwise making available payment stablecoins in the United States." The document asks commenters whether the proposed approach is appropriate "or whether, in the alternative, these regulations should adopt an approach that is more similar to existing securities or commodities regulatory frameworks, such as Regulation S under the Securities Act," and states that "While informed by Regulation S concepts, such an approach need not import Regulation S wholesale." Numbered questions ask whether the proposed definitions of "located in the United States" and "United States" are clear and whether they are under- or over-inclusive, and whether issuance in the United States should turn on the location of the parties or on "other, broader measures of nexus to the United States during the issuance process, such as the use of U.S. financial institutions, payment rails, or other infrastructure." The Federal Register DATES section states that "Comments on the NPRM must be received on or before October 19, 2026." Treasury's accompanying press release states that beginning on January 18, 2027, the expected effective date of the GENIUS Act, a person generally may not issue a payment stablecoin in the United States without an appropriate federal or state license, and that beginning on July 18, 2028 digital asset service providers generally may not offer or sell payment stablecoins to persons in the United States unless issued by a licensed issuer. The release states the NPRM builds on an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Treasury issued in September 2025.

items.issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission
items.title: FTC announces $2.1 million stipulated final order against bill payment platform Doxo and two co-founders over search-ad biller impersonation, undisclosed fees and subscription charges
items.facts: On August 17, 2026 the Federal Trade Commission announced that online bill payment firm Doxo will pay $2.1 million to settle allegations that the company and two of its co-founders, Steve Shivers and Roger Parks, "used misleading search ads to impersonate consumers' billers and misled consumers about millions of dollars in fees they tacked on to consumers' bills." The FTC's 2024 complaint alleged the defendants used search ads and other advertisements "to trick consumers into using Doxo's third-party bill payment platform to pay utility, car loan and other bills by disguising itself as the official payment channel for those bills," that Doxo's landing page "often featured other companies' names and sometimes even their logos," and that Doxo "did not, however, have a relationship with the overwhelming majority of the companies it claimed were part of its payment network." The FTC alleged Doxo added "delivery fees" that were not clearly disclosed and "deceptively signed consumers up for its recurring subscription program." The Commission states that "At the request of the FTC, a federal court found that Doxo violated the Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act for failing to clearly disclose subscription terms and failing to obtain consumers' consent for subscription charges." Under the proposed order the $2.1 million "will be used for consumer redress," and Doxo, Shivers and Parks are prohibited from misrepresenting their affiliation with billers, from using a biller's website address in any search advertisement or using a biller's branded name or logo in a manner that misrepresents affiliation, from misrepresenting amounts consumers will pay or the nature, purpose or total of any fee, from using false representations to obtain a customer's financial information, from misrepresenting a negative option feature including the ability to cancel, and from charging consumers without obtaining their expressed informed consent. The Commission vote approving the stipulated final order was 2-0 and the proposed order was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington. The FTC notes that stipulated final orders have the force of law when approved and signed by the District Court judge.

items.issuing_body: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
items.title: CFPB ceases discretionary publication of consumer complaint narratives and data visualizations, moving previously published narratives to its FOIA reading room
items.facts: On August 14, 2026 the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau announced that it "is ceasing publication of unverified complaint narratives and visualizations." The Bureau states that "the publication in the Consumer Complaint Database of unverified complaint narratives and associated data visualizations is entirely discretionary" and that "Many years of experience have demonstrated that the utility of such publication is minimal, while often causing confusion and providing misleading data." The announcement states that complaint narratives "reflect negative consumer experiences and present only one side of an issue," that "these unverified allegations do not always describe violations of the law and the complaint process does not verify the allegations in each consumer's complaint narrative, nor can it, as a practical matter," and that publication "also needlessly harms companies' reputations." On the existing material the Bureau states: "The Bureau considers previously published narratives to be in the public domain for Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) purposes. Like the Federal Trade Commission, the Bureau is placing these narratives and is proactively disclosing them in the CFPB's FOIA Reading Room." The Bureau states it "remains committed to meeting its statutory obligations and will continue to collect, monitor, and respond to consumers' complaints, to systematically review and assess how well companies are providing complete, accurate, and timely responses, to share consumer complaint information securely with prudential regulators, FTC, other federal and state agencies, and to disclose certain data in response to FOIA requests."

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC proposes Regulation Crypto Assets, with two offering exemptions and a conditional investment-contract safe harbor
items.facts: On August 18, 2026 the SEC announced it proposed new rules, titled Regulation Crypto Assets, that would create a framework for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets. The proposal includes a one-time exemption from Securities Act registration permitting offerings of up to $5 million during a four-year period, and a second exemption permitting offerings of up to $75 million during each 12-month period. Under both exemptions issuers would be required to make certain principles-based narrative disclosures available to investors, and issuers under the second exemption would also be required to provide financial statements and be subject to ongoing reporting requirements. The proposal further includes a conditional safe harbor from the term investment contract in the definitions of security in the Securities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and would preempt state securities law registration and qualification requirements for securities issued under a Regulation Crypto Assets exemption as well as certain secondary market transactions. The public comment period will remain open for 60 days following publication of the proposing release in the Federal Register.

items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC proposes part 4 amendments adding CPO and CTA registration exemptions and raising the small pool threshold
items.facts: On August 18, 2026 the CFTC published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeking public comments on amendments to part 4 of the CFTC's regulations, addressing registration requirements for commodity pool operators and commodity trading advisors, with the stated aim of reducing duplicative and overlapping regulation. The proposed rule would add an exemption from CPO registration for certain investment advisers registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission in relation to commodity pools for which the participants are limited to certain sophisticated investors and which meet other conditions discussed in the proposal, add a related registration exemption for commodity trading advisors, and increase the capital contribution threshold in the current CPO registration exemption for small commodity pools, known as the small pool exemption, to reflect inflation. Comments will be accepted for 45 days following publication in the Federal Register.

items.issuing_body: King County Superior Court, State of Washington
items.title: Washington court orders KalshiEX to stop offering sports, elections, politics, culture, tech and mentions contracts in the state and to geofence by August 19 and September 2
items.facts: On August 12, 2026, King County Superior Court Judge John F. McHale signed an Amended and Updated Order Granting Plaintiff State of Washington's Amended Motion for Preliminary Injunction in State of Washington v. KalshiEX, LLC, No. 26-2-10264-3 SEA. The Washington State Office of the Attorney General announced the order on August 13, 2026. The order directs that Kalshi "shall cease marketing, advertising, promoting, conducting, operating, facilitating, distributing, offering, or accepting event contracts, or other contracts, instruments, or products in Washington, related to sports, elections, politics, entertainment, culture, tech and science, or mentions," and states that this "does not include bets in the following categories, 'Commodities,' 'Climate,' Economics,' and 'Finance.'" It further orders that "By no later than August 19, 2026 Kalshi will implement IP address and residency based geofencing, and by no later than September 2, 2026, Kalshi will implement a multi-source geofencing solution provided through GeoComply," while providing that "Kalshi will not prohibit users from exiting positions they already hold." If implementation with GeoComply is not complete by September 2, 2026, the order states that Kalshi will either pay the State $120,000.00 each day thereafter until implementation is complete or submit a sworn affidavit explaining why implementation remains incomplete, with penalties in an amount to be determined by the Court if it finds insufficient diligence. The order also requires Kalshi to preserve records reasonably related to Washington consumers, including geolocation determinations and marketing and targeting data, to maintain the status quo as to transaction fees obtained from consumers who identified or self-reported as Washingtonians, and to provide Washington the same GeoComply implementation information it provides to Michigan and Nevada. On preemption, the order concludes that "The Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) does not preempt Washington State gambling law," that 7 U.S.C. 2(a)(1)(A) "does not contain express preemption language," that "while the CEA preempts the field of regulating on DCMs, it does not preempt the State of Washington's enforcement of gambling law under RCW 9.46," and that "The impartial access rule does not require Kalshi to violate state law," describing 17 C.F.R. 38.151(b) as a non-discrimination provision. It finds that the State has shown a likelihood that Kalshi's conduct violates multiple provisions of the Washington Gambling Act and that "Kalshi's provision, marketing, and advertising of illegal gambling activities constitute unfair and/or deceptive acts or practices in trade or commerce under RCW 19.86.020." The order records that on December 9, 2025 the Washington State Gambling Commission issued a notice stating that offering events-based contracts or participating in these markets is not authorized in Washington State, and that Kalshi is subject to a preliminary injunction in Nevada. This is a preliminary injunction entered on a likelihood-of-success standard, not a final judgment on the merits.

items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract exchanges, sportsbook and sweepstakes operators, geolocation and compliance vendors

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC staff advisory sets expectations for prediction-market incentive-program self-certifications
items.facts: On August 12, 2026 the CFTC's Division of Market Oversight issued Staff Advisory 26-23, announced as Release 9282-26, reminding designated contract markets of their obligations under the Commodity Exchange Act and Part 40 of the Commission's regulations when submitting rule self-certifications for market-maker, liquidity, trading or incentive programs under Rules 40.5 and 40.6. The advisory states that staff have observed an increase in incentive-program rule filings relating to event contract products that are "procedurally or substantively deficient." It states that volume-based rewards with steep tiers or threshold bonuses "can encourage participants to trade solely to reach volume targets, heightening risks of wash-trading, pre-arranged trading, or other fraudulent, manipulative, or disruptive trading practices," that market-maker programs guaranteeing net profits or covering participant losses "may incentivize artificial strategies," and that "sweepstakes-like or randomized rewards programs or prizes based, in whole or in part, on pure chance, rather than pre-defined performance metrics, likely run afoul of Core Principle 2." A footnote adds that rewards "should not be offered through gamified, casino-style, or other chance-based mechanisms, including spin-the-wheel promotions." DMO staff recommend that all designated contract markets that have previously submitted incentive programs under Rule 40.6(a) review those programs for compliance and submit amendments reasonably within the scope of the advisory under Rule 40.6(a) or Rule 40.6(d) by September 14, 2026. The advisory states that it is informational, does not create new obligations, and represents only the views of DMO staff.
items.source_label: CFTC Release 9282-26 and DMO Staff Letter No. 26-23 (August 12, 2026)

items.issuing_body: SEC
items.title: SEC publishes Nasdaq ISE proposal to set listing criteria for options on trusts holding digital commodities
items.facts: The SEC published on August 13, 2026 a notice of filing of a proposed rule change by Nasdaq ISE, LLC, Release No. 34-106067, File No. SR-ISE-2026-42, at 91 FR 52387. The filing would amend ISE Options 4, Section 3 to adopt listing criteria for options on Commodity-Based Trusts that hold one or more digital commodities. It replaces the term "crypto asset" with "digital commodity," defined as a commodity that is a digital asset and is "intrinsically linked to, and derives its value from, the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system, as well as supply and demand dynamics, rather than from the expectations of profits from the essential managerial efforts of others." The exchange states that this definition "is informed by the joint interpretative guidance issued by the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, effective March 23, 2026," published at 91 FR 13714. Under the proposal each underlying digital commodity must have a total global supply with an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months, and up to 15 percent of the trust's net asset value in the aggregate may consist of digital commodities that do not underlie a derivatives contract trading on a market covered by a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement. The notice states the exchange has comprehensive surveillance sharing agreements with CME and Coinbase Derivatives through common membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group. Comments are due on or before September 3, 2026.

items.issuing_body: City of Baltimore (Mayor and City Council; Baltimore City Law Department)
items.title: Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket under the city consumer protection ordinance over prediction-market sports wagering
items.facts: On August 13, 2026 Mayor Brandon M. Scott and the City Council of Baltimore filed lawsuits in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City against prediction market operators Kalshi and Polymarket and their affiliated companies. According to the City's announcement, the suits allege the companies violated Baltimore's Consumer Protection Ordinance by operating illegal, unlicensed sports-betting platforms and misleading consumers about the legality and regulatory status of their products. The City states that the complaints allege the platforms let Baltimore residents wager on game winners, point spreads, point totals, player statistics and other propositions commonly offered by licensed sportsbooks, and that although the companies describe these wagers as event contracts or prediction-market trades, the complaints contend they function as sports bets and constitute unlawful gambling under Maryland law. The City asserts claims for unfair, abusive and deceptive trade practices and seeks civil penalties, injunctive relief, restitution for affected consumers, disgorgement of profits and other relief authorized by law. City Solicitor Ebony M. Thompson is quoted saying the companies cannot circumvent Baltimore's consumer protections by repackaging gambling as something else or claiming federal regulation puts them beyond the reach of city laws. The complaints themselves are hosted by outside counsel and were not retrieved for this entry.

items.issuing_body: New York Attorney General and New York State Department of Financial Services
items.title: New York conditions Western Union's Intermex acquisition on three years of branch, corridor and pricing commitments
items.facts: On August 13, 2026 New York Attorney General Letitia James and NYDFS Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow announced an agreement with The Western Union Company tied to DFS approval of Western Union's acquisition of International Money Express, Inc. (Intermex), memorialized in an Assurance of Discontinuance filed by the Office of the Attorney General. For three years Western Union must maintain at least the same physical presence in ZIP codes where Intermex locations operate at the time of the acquisition, offer retail remittance services for New York customers to Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru at each of those locations, and limit price increases on retail services to only those that keep pace with inflation. Western Union must report to DFS for three years on service terminations and their reasons, on customer communications regarding availability and pricing, and on the number and amount of retail and digital remittances per location by method and destination country together with fee schedules, and must pay for an independent, DFS-approved auditor to conduct an audit one year after the acquisition. The announcement states the Attorney General will be able to take enforcement action or extend the terms of the agreement if Western Union is found to have breached them. It cites roughly 3,000 Western Union licensed agent locations in New York and states Intermex serves more than 6,000 New York consumers per year.

items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC publishes agenda for the inaugural Innovation Advisory Committee meeting on crypto, AI and prediction markets
items.facts: On August 13, 2026 CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig released the agenda for the inaugural meeting of the Innovation Advisory Committee, scheduled for Thursday, August 20, 2026 from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm Eastern and to be streamed live on CFTC.gov (release 9283-26). The release states that attendees will discuss topics related to the regulation of crypto assets, artificial intelligence, and prediction markets. The published agenda lists three sessions. Session I, Crypto's Regulatory Evolution: From Uncertainty to Clarity, lists potential topics including the evolution of state licensing regimes and the resulting patchwork of requirements, the absence of a comprehensive federal market structure framework, the impact of overlapping jurisdictions and regulation-by-enforcement policymaking, and opportunities to modernize existing rules using current statutory authority. Session II, Artificial Intelligence: Preparing for Intelligent Markets, lists the rise of agentic finance, autonomous agents capable of executing financial transactions, and the intersection of crypto and AI. Session III, Prediction Markets: Innovation, Jurisdiction, and the Future of Event Contracts, lists the respective roles of federal and state authorities in overseeing prediction markets, recent state litigation and enforcement actions, product design principles for event contracts, and expectations for exchanges listing innovative products. Members of the public may submit comments in connection with the meeting by August 27 through Regulations.gov docket CFTC-2026-1717-0001. The meeting notice appears at 91 FR 51697. The release states the agenda may change and that the views expressed by the Advisory Committees are solely those of the respective Committee.

items.issuing_body: Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC exercises emergency authority after KalshiEX reports a market emergency, ordering the exchange to keep operating amid the New York Attorney General's suit
items.facts: The CFTC announced on August 11, 2026 (Release 9281-26) that it "exercised its emergency authority in response to KalshiEX, LLC's notification of a market emergency and ordered the exchange to continue to operate in accordance with the Commodity Exchange Act's Core Principles." The Commission states that KalshiEX notified it of the emergency after New York Attorney General Letitia James filed a complaint against the exchange in state court on July 31, in which, per the release, "New York seeks a temporary restraining order prohibiting KalshiEX, LLC from offering all event contracts nationwide and more than $36 billion in damages." Chairman Michael S. Selig is quoted saying that "Congress did not intend for derivatives exchanges to be regulated under a patchwork of state gaming laws" and that "New York has no business regulating these interstate financial markets." The release states that the CFTC has filed lawsuits against Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island and Wisconsin, and has filed amicus briefs in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth and Ninth Circuits and the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts. An Emergency Order titled "Market Emergency Declaration" dated August 11, 2026 is linked from the release.

items.issuing_body: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), U.S. Department of the Treasury
items.title: FinCEN issues a final rule permanently ending Corporate Transparency Act beneficial-ownership reporting for U.S. companies and U.S. persons, and will delete data already reported
items.facts: Treasury announced on August 11, 2026 (release sb0603) that FinCEN "is issuing a final rule that permanently removes the requirement for U.S. companies and U.S. persons to report beneficial ownership information to FinCEN under the Corporate Transparency Act," and that "The final rule is effective on its publication in the Federal Register." Treasury states that FinCEN "will delete previously reported information by U.S. persons—now exempt from the reporting requirements—from the beneficial ownership information database." Per the release, the final rule adopts the exemptions set out in the March 2025 interim final rule and makes the rollback permanent; exempts U.S. persons holding FinCEN IDs from any obligation to update or correct the information they provided to obtain them; eliminates the requirement for foreign companies to report U.S.-person "company applicants"; exempts foreign pooled investment vehicles registered in the United States from reporting a controlling U.S. person; and confirms deletion of information about any individual FinCEN reasonably believes is a U.S. person. The release states that "Under the final rule, foreign entities that are reporting companies will still be required to report beneficial ownership information for foreign individuals," and that FinCEN has issued Frequently Asked Questions. As of the August 12, 2026 Federal Register issue, the rule had not yet appeared in the Federal Register.

items.issuing_body: Commodity Futures Trading Commission; U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: CFTC and SEC file parallel complaints against Goliath Ventures and CEO Christopher Delgado over an alleged crypto-asset Ponzi scheme, following a criminal guilty plea in June
items.facts: On August 11, 2026 the CFTC announced (Release 9280-26) that it filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida against Goliath Ventures Inc. and CEO Christopher Delgado, alleging "a Ponzi scheme by fraudulently soliciting and accepting funds from the public for crypto asset trading, including in bitcoin and ether," and stating that "approximately 1,600 customers contributed at least $397 million to the defendants' fraud." The CFTC seeks restitution, disgorgement, civil monetary penalties, trading and registration bans and a permanent injunction. The same day the SEC filed its own complaint in the same court (Litigation Release No. 26608), stating that the defendants raised "at least $425 million from over 1,300 investors" through an unregistered securities offering in which investors would "partner" with Goliath to invest in "purported crypto asset liquidity pools," with promised monthly distributions of 3% to 10% and guaranteed return of principal. The SEC alleges that no investor funds or crypto assets were ever placed into any liquidity pool and that Delgado misappropriated at least $51 million. The SEC charges Securities Act Sections 5(a), 5(c) and 17(a) and Exchange Act Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5, and charges Delgado under Exchange Act Section 15(a)(1); Delgado has consented to a bifurcated settlement subject to court approval. The CFTC release states that Delgado pleaded guilty to related federal criminal charges in June 2026 in a case brought by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Florida. The two agencies' complaints state different victim counts and dollar figures, as quoted above.

items.issuing_body: Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC renews its Innovation Advisory Committee for two years, stating that its anti-fraud and anti-manipulation authority covers certain crypto assets
items.facts: The CFTC published a notice of renewal in the Federal Register on August 12, 2026 (91 FR 52047, document 2026-16423) announcing the renewal of the Innovation Advisory Committee and stating that "The Commission has determined that the renewal of the IAC is necessary and in the public's interest." The notice states that the committee "will operate for two years from the date of renewal unless the Commission directs that the IAC terminate on an earlier date." In its Commission-approved public interest determination the CFTC states that "Innovations that may significantly impact our markets include those involving blockchain technologies, artificial intelligence, machine learning, prediction markets, and cybersecurity innovations," and that "The CFTC has statutory anti-fraud and anti-manipulation authority over commodities, which includes certain crypto assets and environmental-based products." The notice records that in FY 2024 the committee approved five recommendations relating to artificial intelligence and six recommendations on decentralized finance, that membership is expected to run to approximately 40-45 uncompensated members drawn from market participants, CFTC registrants, financial technology providers, market infrastructure firms, self-regulatory organizations, public interest groups and academics, and that estimated annual operating cost is $83,581.88. The notice is dated August 10, 2026 and signed by Christopher Kirkpatrick, Secretary of the Commission. The committee's next meeting is scheduled for August 20, 2026, with written public statements due August 27, 2026.

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC charges Regulation Crowdfunding platform operator Netcapital and five individuals with overstating revenue by roughly 345 percent through sham consulting agreements
items.facts: SEC Litigation Release No. 26607, dated August 11, 2026, announces that on August 10, 2026 the Commission filed charges in federal district court in Boston against Netcapital Inc. and five affiliated individuals "for allegedly participating in a fraudulent scheme to overstate Netcapital's revenue while raising more than $25 million from investors." The release states that "from approximately October 2021 through January 2024, Netcapital improperly recognized nearly $14 million in revenue from sham consulting agreements, some of which were forged, which amounted to Netcapital overstating its revenue by approximately 345 percent," and that the inflated revenue appeared in public SEC filings and securities offering materials. Per the release, "The alleged fraudulent scheme involved a Netcapital subsidiary that purportedly entered into consulting agreements with startups or other small companies seeking investment from the public under SEC Regulation Crowdfunding (Reg. CF)," and "the consulting agreements were fictitious." The named defendants alongside the company are John Fanning, Coreen Kraysler, Martin Kay, Paul Riss and Cecilia Lenk. The complaint charges anti-fraud, reporting, certification and books-and-records provisions and seeks permanent and conduct-based injunctions, disgorgement, officer-and-director bars and civil penalties. Lenk consented to a final judgment, subject to court approval, including permanent injunctions and a $50,000 civil penalty.
items.source_label: SEC Litigation Release No. 26607 (August 11, 2026)

items.issuing_body: New York State Department of Financial Services
items.title: NYDFS alerts all DFS-regulated entities to an active campaign exploiting the N-central remote monitoring vulnerability
items.facts: The New York State Department of Financial Services issued an Industry Letter dated August 11, 2026, addressed to all DFS-regulated entities and captioned “Cybersecurity Threat Alert – N-central Vulnerability.” The letter states that DFS is issuing the alert regarding an active cybersecurity campaign targeting a security vulnerability in the remote monitoring and management system N-central, developed and maintained by N-able, which is used by some managed service providers to centrally monitor, patch, and remotely access their customers’ services and endpoints. According to the letter, threat actors are targeting a Known Exploited Vulnerability in N-central to compromise managed service provider environments; once access is obtained, threat actors may create or register for new services, allowing continued access even after compromised N-central credentials are revoked; and attackers are using a compromised provider’s environment to move laterally into their customer’s networks and information systems with administrator network privileges. DFS states that regulated entities should promptly determine whether N-central is used within their environment or by any managed service provider or other third-party service provider that supports their information systems, and, where it is used, work with those providers to review N-central activity for evidence of unauthorized or persistent access, verify that applicable security updates and other mitigation steps have been implemented, and evaluate whether any systems or credentials were affected. The letter states that the senior governing bodies and senior officers of DFS-regulated entities must actively engage in cybersecurity risk management, including through monitoring and oversight of third-party service providers, and that entities should ensure they continue to report all Cybersecurity Incidents to DFS, including those originating at third-party service providers, as required by 23 NYCRR § 500.17. The letter links N-able’s August 6, 2026 security update, the records for CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577, and the Department’s October 21, 2025 guidance on managing risks related to third-party service providers.

items.title: DOJ announces Arms Export Control Act guilty plea in which roughly $30,000 in USDT was paid for export-controlled military communications hardware
items.facts: The U.S. Department of Justice announced on August 10, 2026, in press release 26-909, that Dingwei Chen, a 29-year-old citizen of the People’s Republic of China, pleaded guilty in federal court in Salt Lake City to violating the Arms Export Control Act. Sentencing is scheduled for October 19 and Chen faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. According to the release, Chen attempted to purchase military-grade satellite modems and radios manufactured for the U.S. military by American companies, hardware that may not be legally exported from the United States without a license from the State Department’s Directorate of Defense Trade Controls, which the release states generally does not issue licenses to export military goods and services to China. On the payment arrangements, the release states that after making an initial down payment of over $40,000 U.S. dollars, Chen and his co-conspirators switched to cryptocurrency, noting that “cold wallets are essentially anonymous bank accounts. Each transaction processed through them is private and untraceable,” and that they went on to pay roughly $30,000 worth of USDT, which the release describes as a type of cryptocurrency; the release states these down payments related to the purchase of 10 modems. The release further states that Chen worked with others in China to acquire the systems from foreign arms dealers on the black market, that the group discussed transshipment through Switzerland, pickup in Saipan and finally smuggling through Mexico, and that they communicated using an encrypted app through which Chen claimed the transaction was an initial deal and that he had funding to buy tens of millions of dollars’ worth of additional military equipment. The case was investigated by ICE Homeland Security Investigations and the Defense Criminal Investigative Service and is being prosecuted by the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section.

items.facts: Treasury and the IRS published final regulations (TD 10053, RIN 1545-BR80, 91 FR 51391) governing backup withholding under Internal Revenue Code section 3406 on reportable payments with respect to third party network transactions. The regulations are effective August 10, 2026 and apply with respect to payments made in calendar years beginning after December 31, 2024. items.facts: In Release 9278-26, dated August 7, 2026, the CFTC stated that its Division of Market Oversight and Market Participants Division "recently issued a letter to remind Commission-regulated entities involved in the listing, soliciting, or acceptance of event contracts of their responsibility not to mislead consumers, including the obligation to display clear and accurate pricing information for derivatives products." The release stated that staff "warned that displaying pricing information in the 'American' odds format used by casino gambling bookmakers is likely to mislead market participants about the nature of the transaction and may deprive users of access to indicia of market depth and pricing impact," and that "displaying misleading pricing information in connection with any regulated product risks violating federal law prohibiting the use of manipulative devices." The underlying letter, addressed to "CFTC-Regulated Entities and Affiliates" under the subject "Misleading or Deceptive Practices" and signed by DJ Hennes, Director of the Market Participants Division and Acting Director of the Division of Market Oversight, cites the prohibition on misleading practices in 7 U.S.C. 9 and Commission Regulation 180.1, notes that the same requirements are "mirrored in other rules governing CFTC-regulated entities and their affiliates, for example in National Futures Association Compliance Rule 2-29," and states that designated contract markets "have an obligation to protect market participants from abusive, noncompetitive, or unfair actions by other parties involved in the transaction" under Core Principle 12. The letter states that the divisions "request that CFTC-regulated entities that list, solicit, or accept orders for event contract derivatives products review their pricing displays, marketing material, and other information, as well as information displayed or used by their partners and affiliates and confirm receipt of this letter by August 31, 2026," directing introducing brokers and futures commission merchants to confirm to MPDAlerts@CFTC.gov and designated contract markets to confirm to DMOLetters@CFTC.gov.

items.facts: On August 7, 2026 the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced that OFAC "is moving against digital asset exchanges that the Iranian regime relies on to launder billions of dollars, maintain covert access to international financial systems, and support the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), among other terrorist groups." Treasury states the action targets two major digital asset exchanges used by Tehran along with the ringleader of a multi-jurisdiction front-company network. Siavash Kayvanpour, who operates Republic of Georgia-based SHPS Shelbit and the Shelbit Exchange, is designated under Executive Order 13224, as amended; Treasury states that digital currency addresses belonging to the IRGC sent the equivalent of over $1 million in digital assets to Shelbit Exchange addresses, that more than the equivalent of $2 million was transferred from Shelbit Exchange addresses to IRGC addresses, and that addresses controlled by Kayvanpour sent over $2 million in digital assets to U.S.-designated Nobitex. Also designated under E.O. 13224 are UAE-based Shelbit General Trading LLC, Poland-based Shelbit Technologies Ltd, and UAE-based Crypto Home DMCC and NFT Home DMCC. Iran-based Aban Tether, which Treasury states has processed millions of dollars' worth of transactions involving previously designated Iranian digital asset exchanges including Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex, is designated under E.O. 13902. The corresponding SDN listing (OFAC recent action 20260807) records Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BNB and Solana addresses across the Kayvanpour, SHPS Shelbit and Crypto Home DMCC entries, and marks the E.O. 13224 entries as carrying secondary sanctions risk under section 1(b) of E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886. Treasury states that all property and interests in property of the designated persons in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC, that entities owned 50 percent or more by blocked persons are also blocked, and that OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. Treasury points to FAQ 1250 and amended FAQ 1257 for sanctions risk associated with Iranian digital asset exchanges, including secondary sanctions risk, and states the action was developed in coordination with IRS-Criminal Investigation.

items.title: NY Attorney General issues consumer alert on "gold bar scams" that move victims' savings out of bank accounts
items.facts: On August 7, 2026 New York Attorney General Letitia James issued a consumer alert warning of "increasingly common 'gold bar scams'" targeting seniors. The alert states the scams "usually start with a fake pop-up message on victims' computers, claiming their computer or financial accounts have been compromised or linked to criminal activity," that scammers "convince the victim to give them remote access to their computer and then persuade the victim to convert their money into gold bars to protect their life savings," and that "These gold bars are later collected and laundered by the scammers." According to the alert, "The New York City Police Department (NYPD) has investigated more than 100 gold bar scam cases over the past two years, with total losses exceeding $100 million." The alert states that victims are connected to "an individual posing as a law enforcement officer or government investigator" who tells them they "must withdraw their savings and purchase gold bars or coins from legitimate dealers and turn these bars over to the purported authorities," that "Victims are instructed to keep the matter confidential and not discuss it with bank employees or family members," and that "The scammers will then use couriers to collect the gold from the victim." Published consumer tips include "Never move money out of your bank account at the urging of someone over the phone" and, if someone claims there is an issue with a bank account, to "hang up and contact your financial institution by calling the number printed on your bank statement instead." The alert directs New York City residents to contact their local NYPD precinct and others to file a complaint with the OAG or call 1-800-771-7755.

items.issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission
items.title: FTC issues a policy statement that it will not pursue disparate-impact or 'unfair discrimination' claims
items.facts: On August 7, 2026 the Federal Trade Commission announced "a policy statement clarifying that the Commission will not pursue claims based on disparate-impact or 'unfair discrimination' theories." Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson is quoted in the release: "Disparate-impact claims are nearly impossible to square with our colorblind Constitution. They impose liability for discrimination without any evidence that anyone intended to discriminate, which pushes businesses to make race-based decisions in order to avoid liability. The Commission never had authority to impose disparate-impact liability. Today, we announce that the Commission will never do so again." The FTC states that the policy statement follows a Presidential executive order on "Restoring Equality of Opportunity and Meritocracy," and that the statement explains the Commission lacks the statutory authority to consider claims under this theory. On what remains, the release states: "The statement sets forth how the Commission will pursue discrimination claims in appropriate contexts. For example, it will continue to assert disparate-treatment claims under the Equal Credit and Opportunity Act, but it will treat Section 5 of the FTC Act as the consumer-protection statute it has always been." The FTC also states that under the new policy it reviewed past decisions based on statistical analyses designed to show disparate-impact liability and entered into agreements to modify certain compliance-related obligations for Napleton Inc., Passport Auto Group and an individual previously associated with Coulter Motor Company LLC. The release states the Commission vote authorizing the policy statement and approving the agreements was 2-0.
